title: Projective affine etale chart covering a flat fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $s\in S$, and suppose $F$ is flat over $S$ at every point of $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist affine schemes $S^{\prime},X^{\prime}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], an elementary etale neighbourhood $e:(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})\to(S,s)$ [def-sfb-scheme-relative-purity], and morphisms $g:X^{\prime}\to X$, $p:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ with $fg=ep$, such that $g$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $X_s\subseteq g(X^{\prime})$, and $\Gamma(X^{\prime},g^*F)$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is projective over $\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Projectivity is not required to have finite rank over the base ring.

proof.text: For each $x\in X_s$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-point-projective-etale-source-chart] to $f,F,x$. The hypotheses hold because finite presentation of $f$ implies local finite presentation, and the assumed relative flatness holds at this $x$. Obtain affine $Y_x,S_x$, elementary etale maps $g_x:(Y_x,y_x)\to(X,x)$ and $e_x:(S_x,s_x)\to(S,s)$, and $q_x:Y_x\to S_x$ with $fg_x=e_xq_x$ and $q_x(y_x)=s_x$. Put $R_x=\Gamma(S_x,\mathcal O)$ and $M_x=\Gamma(Y_x,g_x^*F)$; the cited theorem makes $M_x$ projective over $R_x$.

Let $h_x=(g_x,q_x):Y_x\to X\times_SS_x$. The projection $X\times_SS_x\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Since its composite with $h_x$ is the etale map $g_x$, cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] makes $h_x$ etale. Using $\kappa(s_x)=\kappa(s)$, base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_x)\to S_x$ gives an etale map $(Y_x)_{s_x}\to X_s$. Its image $V_x$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and contains $x$, because $y_x$ lies over $s_x$. The fibre $X_s$ is quasi-compact: base change the quasi-compact morphism $f$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ using [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], and evaluate over the whole affine base. Thus the open cover $(V_x)$ has a finite subcover $V_{x_1},\ldots,V_{x_n}$ by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. We retain the distinguished fibres, rather than all points of $Y_x$ over $s$.

source.place: Tag 05KW, finite-subcover paragraph; distinguished-fibre version makes the subsequent coverage assertion explicit.

proof.text: Write $S_i=S_{x_i}$ and $s_i=s_{x_i}$. Construct a common elementary etale neighbourhood as follows (the finite-cone argument of Tag 057B). Form $T=S_1\times_S\cdots\times_SS_n$. Repeated base change and composition of etale maps make $T\to S$ and its projections to $S_i$ etale. The canonical maps $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S_i$ at $s_i$ give a map to $T$ by the fibre-product universal property. If $t$ is its image, the induced field maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)\to\kappa(s)$ compose to the identity; the second is injective and its image contains all of $\kappa(s)$, so both are isomorphisms. Choose an affine open $S^{\prime}\subseteq T$ containing $t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and write $s^{\prime}=t$. Open immersions are etale, so $e:(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})\to(S,s)$ is elementary, with pointed etale maps $u_i:S^{\prime}\to S_i$. If $n=0$, take $T=S$ and an affine open neighbourhood of $s$ instead. This construction uses only finite pullbacks, the indicated field-map calculation, and an affine open shrink.

source.place: Tag 057B (lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhoods), finite common-cone assertion; flat.tex Tag 05KW, common affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: Put $Y_i=Y_{x_i}$, $Z_i=Y_i\times_{S_i}S^{\prime}$, and $X^{\prime}=\coprod_{i=1}^n Z_i$, with $p:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ and $g|_{Z_i}=g_{x_i}\operatorname{pr}_{Y_i}$. Each $Z_i$ is affine: apply [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] to the singleton affine family $Y_i$ over the affine $S_i$. The projection $Z_i\to Y_i$ is etale since it is the base change of $u_i$, so $Z_i\to X$ is etale by composition. The coproduct map $g$ is etale by [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale], and $X^{\prime}$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum]. The coproduct universal property defines $p$ and $g$, and $fg=ep$ follows on every summand from $fg_{x_i}=e_{x_i}q_{x_i}$. The same construction covers $n=0$: the empty coproduct is affine and its morphism to $X$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 05KW, construction of the finite coproduct after common base change.

proof.text: The pointed map $u_i$ induces the isomorphism $\kappa(s_i)\simeq\kappa(s^{\prime})$, because both fields identify with $\kappa(s)$ through the structure maps. The fibre-product universal property therefore identifies $Z_i\times_{S^{\prime}}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s^{\prime})$ with $Y_i\times_{S_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)=(Y_i)_{s_i}$, compatibly with the maps to $X$. Explicitly both iterated pullbacks classify a map to $Y_i$ together with a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ whose composites to $S_i$ agree; their inverse maps preserve these two projections. Hence the image of $Z_i\to X$ contains $V_{x_i}$. Since those images cover $X_s$, we obtain $X_s\subseteq g(X^{\prime})$; for the empty fibre this inclusion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 05KW, assertion that the constructed map covers the fibre; expanded by the distinguished-fibre pullback calculation.

proof.text: Set $R^{\prime}=\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O)$, $R_i=\Gamma(S_i,\mathcal O)$ and $M_i=\Gamma(Y_i,g_{x_i}^*F)$. The sheaf $g_{x_i}^*F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Pullback composition identifies $(g^*F)|_{Z_i}$ with $\operatorname{pr}_{Y_i}^*(g_{x_i}^*F)$ by [def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply [lem-pc-flat-affine-base-change-sections] with affine base $S_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $X=W=Y_i$, base extension $R_i\to R^{\prime}$, and $W^{\prime}=Z_i$. It gives an $R^{\prime}$-linear isomorphism $N_i:=\Gamma(Z_i,(g^*F)|_{Z_i})\simeq R^{\prime}\otimes_{R_i}M_i$. Each $M_i$ is projective by Step 1, so each $N_i$ is projective by [lem-trf-local-projective-tensor-base-change]. This uses no finite generation or finite presentation of $M_i$ over $R_i$.

source.place: Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), affine computation; flat.tex Tag 05KW, displayed section formula; algebra.tex Tag 05A3 (lemma-ascend-properties-modules), clause (4).

proof.text: The disjoint open coproduct summands cover $X^{\prime}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The sheaf gluing axiom identifies $\Gamma(X^{\prime},g^*F)$ with $\prod_{i=1}^n N_i$: there is no compatibility condition on distinct summands, whose intersections are empty. The scalar action is componentwise through $p$. This finite product is projective by the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]: for a surjection $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ and a linear map $v:\prod_iN_i\to B$, lift each restriction $v\iota_i:N_i\to B$ to $w_i:N_i\to A$ using projectivity, and define $w((m_i))=\sum_iw_i(m_i)$. Then its composite to $B$ is $v$, since $(m_i)=\sum_i\iota_i(m_i)$. For $n=0$ the section module is zero and the unique zero lift works. Thus the constructed data have every required property.

source.place: Tag 05KW, displayed finite direct sum and final projectivity assertion; algebra.tex Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), lifting characterization.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-0bdaa35bb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Item-only S1 split of Stacks 05KW (flat.tex lemma-finite-presentation-flat-along-fibre). I read the statement and the full proof; the statement is unchanged and matches the source clause by clause, with no finite-rank restriction. No new nodes. The only other 05KW-citing node is lem-sfb-finitely-presented-flat-point-projective-etale-neighbourhood, which states Tag 05ME, so it is not a duplicate. Step 1 uses only the statement of the 05ID chart node (lem-sfb-flat-point-projective-etale-source-chart); its hypotheses are lfp ⊂ fp and pointwise flatness, from the equivalent form of def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over. Step 2 uses the images of the distinguished fibres (Y_x)_{s_x}→X_s: this is an étale base change by pasting with κ(s_x)=κ(s), the images are open, and X_s is quasi-compact by qc base change to a point. This correctly sharpens Stacks' 'by construction'. Step 3 writes out the 057B finite cone: T=S_1×_S…×_S S_n, the point t comes from Spec κ(s), and κ(t)→κ(s) is an isomorphism because the composite κ(s)→κ(t)→κ(s) is the identity; then an affine open shrink. Step 4: Z_i is affine (lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change with r=1), Z_i→X is étale by base change of u_i and composition, the finite coproduct is étale and affine, and fg=ep holds summandwise. Step 5: Z_i×_{S'}κ(s')≅(Y_i)_{s_i} over X, so X_s⊆g(X'). Step 6: lem-pc-flat-affine-base-change-sections with R=R_i, S=R', W=Y_i, W'=Z_i gives R'⊗M_i; projectivity transfers by the Mathlib leaf. Step 7: sections over the finite disjoint coproduct are the product, and the explicit lift shows the product is projective. Edge cases checked: empty fibre/n=0, F=0, non-closed s, non-separated S, A^1_k with infinite rank. The four off-unit tools (finite-affine tensor base change, étale coproduct, affine section base change, pullback quasi-coherence) are already declared in split_report.tool_uses, and I accept them as generic black boxes. Nothing cites SGA.
